THE CLAUSE

Models should obey developer instructions unless overridden by root or system instructions.

CLAUSES IT CROSS-REFERENCES

3. **Developer**: Model Spec "developer" sections and developer messages

The levels of authority are as follows

Here is the ordering of authority levels. Each section of the spec, and message role in the input conversation, is designated with a default authority level.

1. **Root**: Model Spec "root" sections
2. **System**: Model Spec "system" sections and system messages
3. **Developer**: Model Spec "developer" sections and developer messages
4. **User**: Model Spec "user" sections and user messages
5. **Guideline**: Model Spec "guideline" sections
6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

Developer: Instructions given by developers using our API.

THE CLAIMS READ OUT OF IT

  C1 models should obey developer instructions
  C2 an instruction from the developer level is overridden by a root instruction that conflicts with it
  C3 an instruction from the developer level is overridden by a system instruction that conflicts with it
  C4 the obligation to obey a developer instruction does not apply when that instruction is overridden by a root or system instruction

EVERY SENTENCE THE TRANSLATION RENDERS BACK

  0. «I is an instruction given by a developer using the OpenAI API, carrying developer-level authority»
  1. «the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts»
  2. «I is an instruction at the root level of authority»
  3. «I is an instruction at the system level of authority»
  4. «instruction I is at authority level L»
  5. «instruction I1 and instruction I2 direct incompatible behavior in the same situation»
  6. I is «I is an instruction at the root level of authority» when «instruction I is at authority level L» and «the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts» (of L, root)
  7. I is «I is an instruction at the system level of authority» when «instruction I is at authority level L» and «the ranking of instruction authority levels: root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts» (of L, system)
  8. clause l1_170_n052 forbids ⟨act obey_instruction(I)⟩ when «I is an instruction given by a developer using the OpenAI API, carrying developer-level authority» and «I is an instruction at the root level of authority» and «instruction I1 and instruction I2 direct incompatible behavior in the same situation»
